newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Sino Land says land bank good for five years.
newsitem.headline: Sino Land says land bank good for five years.

text.p: Sino Land Company Ltd said on Wednesday it has a land bank sufficient to satisfy its development needs for the coming five years and will continue to focus on property development in Hong Kong.

"In the interim period, five sites and one luxury residential building with an aggregate 1,791,427 square feet of gross floor area were acquired," said chairman Robert Ng in the company's earnings report for the six months ended December 31, 1996.
Sino Land announced profit attributable to shareholders of HK$764.6 million (US$98.78 million), a 49.32 percent increase over the corresponding period last year.
The company acquired a 50 percent interest in a large site on Hong Kong island at a government land auction held on Tuesday. Ng's family bought the other half.
The purchase price of HK$11.82 billion was the highest ever paid for a single site at a government auction.

"On completion, this project will consist of 2.5 million square feet of luxury seaview flats and a shopping centre with approximately 1,000 car parking spaces on top of a public transport terminus," Ng said in the statement.

In the past six months, the company also contracted to acquire a large commercial shopping centre in the heart of Hong Kong's tourist district. This acquisition was to be completed by September, he said.
Sino Land also took a 30 percent stake in the Conrad Hotel in Hong Kong, after sister company Sino Hotels Ltd acquired a 50 percent interest in the hotel.
During the six-month period, Sino Land booked the sales of several large residential developments.

"During the six months to December 31, 1996, total property sales were HK$1,402 million," the chairman's statement said, adding that sales in the first two months of 1997 had already reached HK$852 million.
The company's large portfolio of rental properties, which rose to 5.8 million square feet during the period, achieved modest growth in rental income to about HK$558 million.
Earnings per share (EPS) rose to HK$0.28, an increase of 40 percent compared with HK$0.20 in first half of 1995/96.
This was due to the placing of 238 million new shares which resulted in a dilution of EPS.
The new shares issued at HK$9.13 per share in December 1996 netted the group a total of HK$2.13 billion, which was used to finance the acquisition and development of Hong Kong properties.
